findings: Cargo feature closure & optionalized SDK dev-dependencies (`crates/mori/Cargo.toml`): `default = ["native"]` preserves default build semantics, while `native` explicitly gates `dep:mori-backend`, `dep:mori-ledger`, `dep:futures`, `dep:rand`, and all 8 formerly unconditional SDK `[dev-dependencies]` (`midnight-ledger`, `midnight-base-crypto`, `midnight-coin-structure`, `midnight-onchain-state`, `midnight-onchain-runtime`, `midnight-storage`, `midnight-transient-crypto`, `midnight-serialize`) promoted to optional `[dependencies]`. Promoting those 8 crates from `[dev-dependencies]` (which Cargo cannot mark optional) to optional `[dependencies]` under `native` is necessary so `cargo test -p mori --no-default-features` does not compile or link the Midnight SDK graph into integration test binaries. Unconditional dependencies of `mori` (`mori-ast`, `mori-checker`, `mori-core` with non-default `midnight-compat-tests` inactive, `mori-diagnostics`, `mori-fmt`, `mori-lexer`, `mori-parser`, `mori-span`, `clap`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha2`, `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tower-lsp`) pull zero `mori-backend`, `mori-ledger`, or `midnight-*` crates (`k256` remains in `mori-core` solely for legacy Core secp256k1 intents). Root `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (`659ca9ca7df02e4ff4e3c2b424fa2d6b95d73e596fdf85d0046df423ced4dbb5`) are unmodified.

Full clap CLI schema & error/exit contract (`crates/mori/src/cli.rs`, `crates/mori/src/commands/mod.rs`, `crates/mori/src/main.rs`, `crates/mori/src/error.rs`): All 23 subcommand variants, `Args` structs, flattened input/output structs (`ActionInput`, `SigningOutputArgs`, `proof_io::Input`, `call_io::Input`, `signed_call_io::Input`, `replay::AuthorizationArgs`), and `SignedProfile` remain unconditionally compiled in both builds. `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "native"), command(after_help = ...))]` adds availability notes only when `native` is disabled, keeping the default/native clap schema and help text unchanged. `commands::native_unavailable<T>()` constructs the real `CliError::Operation { code: "mori::command::native-unavailable".into(), message: "This mori build has no Midnight support. Rebuild with the native feature enabled.".into() }` constructor, which `main.rs` prints to stderr via `shell.report(&report)` and exits with `ExitCode::FAILURE` (exit 1), while clap syntax/conflict/missing-required errors exit 2 prior to command dispatch.

Native-only command & helper isolation with literal body preservation (`compile`, `compile_call`, `keygen_call`, `keygen_signed_call`, `prepare_call`, `prepare_signed_call`, `prove`, `prove_call`, `prove_signed_call`, `replay`, `verify`, `verify_call`, `verify_signed_call`, `call_io`, `core_io`, `proof_io`, `signed_call_io`): Every native implementation item, helper, and unit test module is gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` / `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]`, with all 103 original top-level function regions preserved verbatim. In `#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]`, each native-only `run` function binds field references (`let _ = (&args...,);`) to satisfy unused-field lints without suppressing real warnings and immediately returns `super::native_unavailable()` before reading any source/target/key/proof file, creating any output directory, or performing any mock/fallback action. `core_io.rs` exposes only pure Core helpers (`read_source`, `parse_and_check`, `read_json`, `write_json`, `operation`, `require_core_one`) unconditionally, keeping `compile_target_artifact`, `read_target_artifact`, and `decode_hex_32` under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`.

Mixed-command validation precedence & zero-fallback refusal (`inspect.rs`, `simulate.rs`, `intent.rs`, `verify_intent.rs`): (a) `inspect`: under `#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]`, `if args.target.is_some() { return super::native_unavailable(); }` runs at the top of `run` before `core_io::read_source(&args.file)`, refusing `inspect --target` even on `moriarty/2` source without reading either the `.mori` file or the target directory; under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`, post-read Core/2 `--target` refusal (`mori::core::profile`) before target read and Core/1 compiled enforcement report remain untouched. (b) `simulate`: clap conflicts (`--logical-cap` with `--trace`, `--resume` with `--trace`/`--target`/etc.) exit 2 first, followed by `args.legacy()` (`--input does not take a value`); inside `if args.trace`, `args.target.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| core_io::operation("--trace requires --target"))` runs first in both builds, and under `#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]` `super::native_unavailable()` is returned immediately before reading target, authority, source, or scenario files; when `!args.trace`, stray `--target` or signed replay flags are still refused with `--target and signed replay arguments require --trace` before reading source. (c) `intent`: when `args.profile.is_some()`, legacy `--scheme`/`--public-key`/`--framing` conflict is checked first, then `signed(args, shell)` checks `let (Some(target), Some(at)) = (&args.target, args.at) else { return Err(super::core_io::operation("--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1 requires --target and --at together")); };` before returning `super::native_unavailable()` in no-native builds without reading source, scenario, target, or authority files, and never reinterpreting JubJub owner intents as secp256k1. (d) `verify-intent`: `match (args.profile, &args.target)` enforces `--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1 requires --target` and `--target belongs to --profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1` first, then calls `signed(&args, target)` which immediately returns `super::native_unavailable()` in no-native builds before any file I/O.
